text:
Exam writers and reviewers for this year's national college entrance exam were set to be released Thursday, after spending some 40 days to produce error-free questions in isolation, continuing the long tradition of the practice repeated each year to preserve the integrity of the high-stakes exam.
According to the Korea Institute for Curriculum and Evaluation (KICE), around 500 test writers and reviewers, along with about 280 administrative staff, began their seclusion at an undisclosed facility in early- to mid-October to craft Thursday's College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT).
They were set to be released after the exam concludes at 5:45 p.m.
Known locally as the Suneung, the CSAT is a pivotal milestone in Korea that heavily influences students' university admissions, future career paths and social standing. Such importance of the exam to many, if not all, students puts immense pressure on the exam writers, who are tasked with creating questions that are completely free of errors while still being creative and effective at distinguishing students. The exam writers are asked to avoid overly tricky questions, but maintain enough difficulty to differentiate top scorers at the same time, according to KICE.
Complete isolation from the outside world apparently adds to the strain during the roughly 40-day camp. Participants were strictly prohibited from leaving the facility or using communication devices such as smartphones, tablets and Bluetooth earphones. Internet access is restricted solely to looking up necessary reference materials for creating and reviewing test questions.
Although the main exam papers were finalized and sent to the printers earlier this month, writers also had to produce a backup set of questions of the same volume in case a natural disaster or emergency forces a postponement of the test, adding further mental and physical exhaustion.
